note.explanation: Data communication is the exchange of data between a sender and a receiver through a medium. The five components tell us who sends the data, who receives it, what is sent, which rules are followed, and how the data travels.
examples: A computer sends an email: the computer is the sender, the smartphone is the receiver, and the email content is the message.
The data may travel through an Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi; these are examples of a medium.
note.simple: Data communication means sending data from one device to another. Remember the five parts: sender, receiver, message, protocol, and medium.
note.checkQuestion: Which component is the set of rules governing data communication?
note.title: The five components of data communication
steps: Identify the device that sends the data: the sender.
Identify the device that receives the data: the receiver.
Identify the data being sent: the message.
Identify the rules for communicating: the protocol.
Identify the path the data travels through: the medium.
note.answer: The five components are sender, receiver, message, protocol, and medium.

options: The path through which data travels
mcqs.stem: Which component is a computer sending an email?
rationales: Correct: the computer is sending the data, so it is the sender.
Incorrect: the receiver is the device that gets the data.
Incorrect: the message is the email content, not the computer.
Incorrect: the medium is the path used to carry the data.

mcqs.stem: A smartphone gets an email sent from a computer. What is the smartphone in this communication?
rationales: Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.
Correct: the smartphone receives the email, so it is the receiver.
Incorrect: the message is the email content.
Incorrect: a protocol is a set of communication rules.

mcqs.stem: In an email communication, which option is the message?
rationales: Incorrect: this is the sender.
Incorrect: this is the receiver.
Correct: the content being communicated is the message.
Incorrect: Wi-Fi is an example of a medium.

options: A set of rules governing data communication
rationales: Correct: a protocol is a set of rules governing data communication.
Incorrect: this describes the sender.
Incorrect: this describes the message.
Incorrect: this describes the medium.

mcqs.stem: An Ethernet cable carries data between devices. Which component does the cable represent?
rationales: Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.
Incorrect: the receiver is the device that gets the data.
Correct: the cable is a path through which data travels, so it is the medium.
Incorrect: the message is the data being communicated.

mcqs.stem: Which component determines the rules followed during data communication?
rationales: Incorrect: the receiver gets the data but does not define the communication rules.
Correct: the protocol is the set of rules governing communication.
Incorrect: the message is the data being communicated.
Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.

mcqs.stem: Which option is an example of a communication medium?
rationales: Correct: Wi-Fi is a wireless path through which data can travel.
Incorrect: email content is an example of a message.
Incorrect: the smartphone is an example of a receiver.
Incorrect: HTTP is an example of a protocol.

explain.title: Data communication
explain.body: Data communication involves the exchange of data between a sender and a receiver through a communication medium.

explain.title: Sender and receiver
explain.body: The sender is the device that sends the data. The receiver is the device that receives it. For example, a computer can send an email to a smartphone.

explain.title: Message
explain.body: The message is the data being communicated. In an email example, the message is the content of the email.

explain.title: Protocol
explain.body: A protocol is a set of rules governing data communication. HTTP is an example used for web communications.

explain.title: Medium
explain.body: The medium is the physical or wireless path through which data travels. An Ethernet cable and Wi-Fi are examples.

mistakes: Do not confuse the message with the medium: the email content is the message, while the cable or Wi-Fi is the medium.
Do not call the device that receives data the sender; identify the direction of data transfer.
Do not describe a protocol as a device or a path; it is a set of rules.
When asked to list the components, include all five: sender, receiver, message, protocol, and medium.
